name: Appendicitis
sx: Pain that starts around the navel and moves to the lower right abdomen
Tenderness that worsens when pressure is released (rebound tenderness)
about: The appendix becomes inflamed, usually after its opening is blocked, often by a small hardened lump of stool called an appendicolith. Trapped bacteria multiply, and without treatment the appendix can burst and infect the abdominal lining (peritonitis). The pain moves because early pain is felt vaguely through gut nerves, then sharpens once inflammation reaches the abdominal wall.

study.title: A Randomized Trial Comparing Antibiotics with Appendectomy for Appendicitis (CODA)
study.note: Antibiotics were noninferior to surgery on a standard health-status measure. Nearly 3 in 10 patients treated with antibiotics still had their appendix removed within 90 days, and an appendicolith raised that risk.

name: Myocardial infarction (heart attack)
sx: Pain spreading to the left arm, jaw, neck or back
about: A coronary artery is blocked, usually when a fatty plaque ruptures and a clot forms on it, and the heart muscle beyond it starts to die from lack of oxygen. Women, older adults and people with diabetes more often have atypical symptoms such as fatigue, nausea or breathlessness without classic chest pain.

study.title: Beta-Blockers after Myocardial Infarction and Preserved Ejection Fraction (REDUCE-AMI)
study.note: In patients whose heart pumping function was preserved after a heart attack, long-term beta-blockers did not lower the risk of death or another heart attack, challenging decades of routine practice.

name: Ischemic stroke
sx: Sudden weakness or numbness on one side of the body
Slurred or garbled speech, or trouble understanding words
Sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes
Sudden loss of balance or coordination
about: A clot blocks an artery supplying the brain. One widely cited estimate is that an untreated large stroke destroys about 1.9 million neurons every minute, which is why the FAST check (Face, Arms, Speech, Time to call) matters. Clot-dissolving drugs and clot retrieval work best when started early.

study.title: Tissue plasminogen activator for acute ischemic stroke (NINDS trial)
study.note: The landmark trial behind clot-busting stroke treatment: IV t-PA given within 3 hours improved outcomes at 3 months despite more brain bleeding.

name: Migraine
sx: Throbbing headache, often on one side
Visual aura before the pain, such as zigzag lines or flashing lights
about: A neurological disorder in which activated trigeminal nerves release inflammatory signaling molecules, notably CGRP, around blood vessels of the brain's coverings. Attacks last 4 to 72 hours. Roughly a quarter to a third of people with migraine get aura. Several newer preventive drugs block CGRP or its receptor.

study.title: Fremanezumab for the Preventive Treatment of Chronic Migraine
study.note: An antibody against CGRP reduced headache frequency compared with placebo over 12 weeks. Injection-site reactions were common.

name: Type 1 diabetes
about: The immune system destroys the insulin-making beta cells of the pancreas. Sugar builds up in the blood and spills into the urine, dragging water with it, which causes thirst and frequent urination. Without insulin the body burns fat for fuel, producing ketones that can cause diabetic ketoacidosis, sometimes noticed as fruity-smelling breath.

study.title: An Anti-CD3 Antibody, Teplizumab, in Relatives at Risk for Type 1 Diabetes
study.note: A 14-day course of the immune-modulating antibody teplizumab delayed the onset of clinical type 1 diabetes in high-risk relatives of patients.

name: Hypothyroidism
about: The thyroid makes too little thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3), so the body's metabolism slows down. In countries with enough dietary iodine, the most common cause is Hashimoto's thyroiditis, an autoimmune attack on the gland. Worldwide, iodine deficiency remains a major cause.

study.title: Thyroid Hormone Therapy for Older Adults with Subclinical Hypothyroidism (TRUST)
study.note: In older adults with mildly abnormal thyroid tests (subclinical hypothyroidism), levothyroxine gave no apparent benefit for symptoms or tiredness.

name: Graves' disease (hyperthyroidism)
sx: Weight loss despite a good appetite
about: An autoimmune disease in which antibodies mimic thyroid-stimulating hormone and switch the thyroid on continuously. The same immune process can inflame the tissue behind the eyes, pushing them forward (Graves' ophthalmopathy). It is the most common cause of hyperthyroidism.

study.title: Smoking and risk of Graves' disease
study.note: Smoking was associated with Graves' disease and especially with more severe eye disease, suggesting it is one trigger in genetically predisposed people.

name: Asthma
sx: Cough, often worse at night or early morning
Symptoms triggered by exercise, cold air or allergens
about: Chronic inflammation makes the airways oversensitive. During an attack the muscles around the airways tighten, the lining swells and mucus builds up, narrowing the passages. Unlike COPD, the narrowing is largely reversible with bronchodilator inhalers.

study.title: Tezepelumab in Adults and Adolescents with Severe, Uncontrolled Asthma (NAVIGATOR)
study.note: Blocking the upstream immune signal TSLP reduced asthma attacks and improved lung function and quality of life compared with placebo.

name: Pneumonia
sx: Sharp chest pain when breathing in
about: An infection fills the lungs' air sacs (alveoli) with fluid and immune cells, which makes oxygen exchange harder. Streptococcus pneumoniae is the classic bacterial cause, but viruses are common too. Older adults may show only confusion or weakness.

study.title: Community-Acquired Pneumonia Requiring Hospitalization among U.S. Adults (EPIC)
study.note: Hospitalization rates were highest in the oldest adults. Despite extensive testing, no pathogen was found in most patients, and viruses were detected more often than bacteria.

name: Pulmonary embolism
sx: Sharp chest pain, worse on breathing in
A swollen, painful leg where the clot started
about: A blood clot, usually from the deep veins of the legs, breaks off and lodges in the arteries of the lungs. It blocks blood flow and strains the right side of the heart. Risk factors include immobility, recent surgery, cancer, pregnancy and estrogen-containing medicines.

study.title: Simplified diagnostic management of suspected pulmonary embolism (the YEARS study)
study.note: A simple three-question checklist plus a D-dimer blood test safely ruled out pulmonary embolism and cut CT scans by an absolute 14%.

name: Gout
sx: Sudden, severe pain in one joint, classically the big toe
Even a bedsheet touching the joint is unbearable
Red, hot skin over the joint
Attacks that often begin at night
about: Uric acid crystallizes in a joint as needle-shaped monosodium urate crystals, and the immune system attacks them, causing intense inflammation. The big toe is a favorite site partly because cooler extremities favor crystal formation. Purine-rich foods, alcohol and some diuretics raise uric acid.

study.title: Cardiovascular Safety of Febuxostat or Allopurinol in Patients with Gout (CARES)
study.note: Febuxostat was noninferior to allopurinol for major cardiovascular events, but all-cause and cardiovascular death were higher with febuxostat.

name: Rheumatoid arthritis
sx: Pain and swelling in the small joints of the hands and feet
The same joints affected on both sides of the body
Morning stiffness lasting more than an hour
Firm lumps under the skin near joints
about: An autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the synovium, the lining of the joints. The inflamed lining thickens and erodes cartilage and bone. Antibodies such as anti-CCP can appear in the blood years before symptoms start.

study.title: Cardiovascular and Cancer Risk with Tofacitinib in Rheumatoid Arthritis (ORAL Surveillance)
study.note: In patients at higher cardiovascular risk, the JAK inhibitor tofacitinib had higher rates of major heart events and cancer than TNF-inhibitor drugs, which led to new safety warnings.

name: Lyme disease
sx: An expanding red rash, often with a bull's-eye pattern
A recent tick bite or time in tick habitat
about: Caused by Borrelia burgdorferi bacteria, spread by blacklegged (Ixodes) ticks. It is named for Lyme, Connecticut, where an unusual cluster of childhood arthritis was investigated in the 1970s. Untreated, it can spread to cause facial palsy, heart rhythm problems or arthritis.

study.title: Antibiotic therapy in Lyme disease
study.note: An early study by Allen Steere's group, who described the disease: penicillin shortened the characteristic rash and significantly fewer treated patients went on to develop arthritis.

name: Bacterial meningitis
sx: A purple rash that doesn't fade when pressed
about: Bacteria infect the meninges, the membranes around the brain and spinal cord. Inflammation raises pressure inside the skull and can damage the brain within hours, so it is a medical emergency. Vaccines against Hib, pneumococcus and meningococcus have made it much rarer.

study.title: Clinical features and prognostic factors in adults with bacterial meningitis
study.note: Fewer than half of adults had the 'classic triad' of fever, neck stiffness and confusion, but almost all had at least two of headache, fever, neck stiffness and altered mental status.

name: Celiac disease
sx: Iron-deficiency anemia that doesn't respond to iron pills
about: In genetically susceptible people (nearly all carry HLA-DQ2 or DQ8), gluten from wheat, barley and rye triggers an immune attack on the small intestine. The finger-like villi flatten, so nutrients like iron are poorly absorbed. The only treatment is a strict lifelong gluten-free diet.

study.title: Association Between Celiac Disease and Mortality Risk in a Swedish Population
study.note: In a nationwide Swedish cohort followed from 1969 to 2017, a celiac diagnosis was associated with a small but statistically significant increase in mortality risk.

name: Iron-deficiency anemia
about: Iron is needed to build hemoglobin, the oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells. With too little, red cells come out small and pale (microcytic and hypochromic), so less oxygen reaches the tissues. Common causes are heavy menstrual bleeding, slow gut bleeding, pregnancy and low intake or absorption.

study.title: Prevalence of Iron Deficiency and Iron-Deficiency Anemia in US Females Aged 12-21 Years, 2003-2020
study.note: Used national survey data to measure how common iron deficiency and anemia are in adolescent girls and young women, to inform future screening strategies.

name: Kidney stones
sx: Severe cramping pain in the side and back, below the ribs
Pain that spreads to the groin
Restlessness, unable to find a comfortable position
about: Minerals in urine, most often calcium oxalate, crystallize into stones. When a stone moves into the narrow ureter, it blocks urine flow and the ureter spasms around it, causing waves of intense pain. Dehydration and certain diets raise the risk.

study.title: Removal of Small, Asymptomatic Kidney Stones and Incidence of Relapse
study.note: Removing small, painless stones during surgery for another stone lowered the rate of relapse without increasing surgery-related emergency visits.

name: Acute cholecystitis
sx: Pain in the upper right abdomen
Pain that catches a deep breath when the area is pressed (Murphy's sign)
Pain spreading to the right shoulder or back
about: Usually a gallstone blocks the cystic duct, the gallbladder's outlet, and the trapped bile inflames the gallbladder wall, sometimes with infection on top. Pain can be felt in the right shoulder because nerves near the diaphragm share pathways with the shoulder (referred pain).

study.title: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy versus percutaneous catheter drainage for acute cholecystitis in high risk patients (CHOCOLATE)
study.note: Even in high-risk patients, keyhole removal of the gallbladder caused fewer major complications than draining it through the skin.

name: Parkinson's disease
sx: Tremor at rest, often a 'pill-rolling' motion of the fingers
A shuffling walk and poor balance
Small handwriting and a soft voice
about: Dopamine-producing neurons in a midbrain region called the substantia nigra die off, and clumps of the protein alpha-synuclein (Lewy bodies) build up. Loss of smell, constipation and acting out dreams during sleep can come years before the movement symptoms.

study.title: Trial of Lixisenatide in Early Parkinson's Disease (LIXIPARK)
study.note: A GLP-1 drug originally developed for diabetes slowed the progression of motor disability over 12 months in a phase 2 trial, with gastrointestinal side effects. Larger trials are needed.

name: Multiple sclerosis
sx: Painful, blurred vision in one eye (optic neuritis)
An electric-shock feeling down the spine when bending the neck (Lhermitte's sign)
Numbness or tingling in the limbs
Symptoms that flare and fade in episodes
about: The immune system attacks myelin, the insulation around nerve fibers in the brain and spinal cord, and scars (scleroses) form in many places over time. Large studies point to Epstein-Barr virus infection as a major risk factor.

study.title: Ofatumumab versus Teriflunomide in Multiple Sclerosis (ASCLEPIOS I and II)
study.note: Ofatumumab, an antibody that depletes B cells, produced lower annual relapse rates than the oral drug teriflunomide, supporting the role of B cells in MS.

name: Influenza (flu)
about: Influenza A and B viruses infect the airways. The abrupt onset, high fever and body aches help tell it apart from a common cold. The virus constantly changes its surface proteins, which is why the vaccine is updated every year.

study.title: Baloxavir Marboxil for Uncomplicated Influenza in Adults and Adolescents (CAPSTONE-1)
study.note: A single dose of baloxavir eased flu symptoms faster than placebo and lowered viral load faster than oseltamivir, though some reduced viral susceptibility emerged.

name: Infectious mononucleosis (mono)
sx: Swollen lymph nodes in the neck
about: Usually caused by Epstein-Barr virus, spread through saliva, most often in teenagers and young adults. The enlarged spleen can rupture, so people are told to avoid contact sports for several weeks. A rash often appears if they are given the antibiotic amoxicillin.

study.title: Characteristics of Hodgkin's lymphoma after infectious mononucleosis
study.note: In young adults, a causal link between mono-related Epstein-Barr infection and the EBV-positive subtype of Hodgkin's lymphoma was found to be likely.

name: Shingles (herpes zoster)
sx: A band-like rash on one side of the body, following one nerve's path
Burning or tingling pain before the rash appears
Nerve pain that lingers after the rash heals
about: Varicella-zoster virus, which causes chickenpox, stays dormant in nerve ganglia for decades. When immunity wanes with age or illness, it reactivates and travels down a single nerve to the skin, so the rash stays on one side and follows that nerve's strip of skin (a dermatome).

study.title: Efficacy of an adjuvanted herpes zoster subunit vaccine in older adults (ZOE-50)
study.note: The recombinant shingles vaccine greatly reduced the risk of shingles in adults 50 and older, with similar efficacy in those over 70.

name: Addison's disease
sx: Darkening of the skin, especially in palm creases and scars
Low blood pressure and dizziness on standing
about: The adrenal cortex is destroyed, usually by autoimmunity, so the body lacks cortisol and aldosterone. The pituitary responds by pumping out ACTH, which is made from the same precursor protein as melanocyte-stimulating hormone, so the skin darkens. President John F. Kennedy had Addison's disease.

study.title: 21-Hydroxylase, a major autoantigen in idiopathic Addison's disease
study.note: Identified the adrenal enzyme 21-hydroxylase as the main target of the autoantibodies in autoimmune Addison's disease. Testing for these antibodies is still used in diagnosis.

name: Cushing's syndrome
sx: A fatty hump between the shoulders
Weight gain in the trunk with thin arms and legs
High blood pressure and high blood sugar
about: Too much cortisol, most often from steroid medications. When the body makes it, the usual cause is a small pituitary tumor driving the adrenals (Cushing's disease), first described by neurosurgeon Harvey Cushing in 1932. Cortisol redistributes fat, breaks down collagen and suppresses immunity.

study.title: Opportunistic infections in endogenous Cushing's syndrome
study.note: Patients with very high cortisol developed opportunistic infections such as cryptococcosis and pneumocystis. Survival depended on bringing cortisol production under control.

name: Peptic ulcer disease
sx: Burning pain in the upper middle abdomen
Black, tarry stools (a sign of bleeding)
Vomiting blood or material like coffee grounds
about: Sores form in the lining of the stomach or duodenum, most often because of Helicobacter pylori infection or NSAID painkillers such as aspirin and ibuprofen. In 1984 Barry Marshall drank a culture of H. pylori to prove it causes stomach inflammation. He and Robin Warren won the 2005 Nobel Prize.

study.title: Helicobacter pylori eradication for primary prevention of peptic ulcer bleeding in older patients prescribed aspirin in primary care (HEAT)
study.note: Clearing H. pylori protected older aspirin users against ulcer bleeding, though the protection may not last in the long term.

name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
sx: Numbness or tingling in the thumb, index and middle fingers
Symptoms worse at night, often waking you up
Relief from shaking out the hand
A weak grip and dropping things
Wasting at the base of the thumb (advanced)
about: The median nerve is squeezed where it passes through a tight tunnel of bone and ligament in the wrist. The little finger is spared because it is supplied by a different nerve, the ulnar nerve. Risk factors include pregnancy, diabetes, hypothyroidism and repetitive forceful wrist use.

study.title: Surgery versus corticosteroid injection for carpal tunnel syndrome (DISTRICTS)
study.note: Starting with surgery gave a higher chance of recovery at 18 months than starting with a steroid injection, even allowing for later additional treatment.

name: Bell's palsy
sx: Sudden weakness of one whole side of the face, including the forehead
Unable to fully close one eye
A drooping corner of the mouth, with drooling
Sounds seem too loud on one side
about: The facial nerve (cranial nerve VII) becomes inflamed and swollen inside its narrow bony canal, probably triggered by a virus. Because the whole nerve is affected, the forehead is paralyzed too. A stroke usually spares the forehead, which is a key clue for telling them apart. Most people recover within months.

study.title: Early treatment with prednisolone or acyclovir in Bell's palsy
study.note: Early prednisolone (a steroid) significantly improved the chance of complete recovery. The antiviral acyclovir added no benefit.

name: Measles
sx: Tiny white spots inside the cheeks (Koplik spots)
A rash that starts on the face and spreads downward
about: Measles is one of the most contagious human viruses: one case can infect 12 to 18 unvaccinated people. It can also cause 'immune amnesia', wiping out existing antibodies to other infections. Two doses of MMR vaccine are about 97% effective.

study.title: Measles, Mumps, Rubella Vaccination and Autism: A Nationwide Cohort Study
study.note: In more than 650,000 Danish children, MMR vaccination did not increase the risk of autism, including in children with risk factors.

name: Deep vein thrombosis
sx: Pain or tenderness in the calf or thigh
about: A clot forms in a deep vein, usually in the leg. Virchow's triad sums up the causes: slow blood flow (such as long flights or bed rest), damage to the vessel wall, and blood that clots too easily. The danger is that a piece breaks off and travels to the lungs as a pulmonary embolism.

study.title: Evaluation of D-dimer in the diagnosis of suspected deep-vein thrombosis
study.note: Philip Wells and colleagues showed that a low clinical probability score plus a negative D-dimer blood test safely ruled out DVT without an ultrasound.

name: Heat stroke
sx: Hot skin, which may be dry or sweating
about: The body's cooling system fails and core temperature climbs high enough to damage the brain and other organs. The change in mental state is what separates it from heat exhaustion. It is an emergency, and rapid cooling such as cold-water immersion saves lives.

study.title: Risk factors for heatstroke. A case-control study
study.note: A study of a US heat wave found that home air conditioning, time in cooled places and drinking extra fluids lowered the risk of heatstroke, while some psychiatric drugs and being unable to care for oneself raised it.

name: Anaphylaxis
sx: Swelling of the lips, tongue or throat
Dizziness or fainting from a drop in blood pressure
Rapid onset within minutes of a trigger such as food, a sting or a drug
about: A severe, whole-body allergic reaction. Allergen binds to IgE antibodies on mast cells, which release histamine and other chemicals all at once, so blood vessels leak and widen and airways tighten. Epinephrine (adrenaline) is the first-line treatment and should be given immediately.

study.title: Food anaphylaxis in the United Kingdom: analysis of national data, 1998-2018
study.note: Hospital admissions for food-induced anaphylaxis rose over two decades while the fatality rate fell. Cow's milk had become the most common single cause of fatal reactions in school-age children.

name: Tuberculosis
sx: A cough lasting three weeks or more
about: Mycobacterium tuberculosis spreads through the air and can lie dormant for years before becoming active. According to the WHO, it has again become the world's leading cause of death from a single infectious agent. Treatment takes months of combined antibiotics.

study.title: Treatment of Highly Drug-Resistant Pulmonary Tuberculosis (Nix-TB)
study.note: An all-oral, three-drug regimen of bedaquiline, pretomanid and linezolid cured a high percentage of patients with highly drug-resistant TB, with some toxic effects.

name: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)
sx: Heartburn: a burning feeling behind the breastbone
Sour liquid rising into the mouth (regurgitation)
Worse after meals or when lying down
about: The lower esophageal sphincter, the valve between the esophagus and stomach, relaxes when it shouldn't, so stomach acid flows back up. Over years, chronic reflux can change the esophageal lining (Barrett's esophagus), which raises cancer risk.

study.title: Association of Acute Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease With Esophageal Histologic Changes
study.note: When 12 patients stopped acid-suppressing drugs, reflux damage began with T-cell inflammation under an intact surface, suggesting immune signaling, not just acid burns, drives the injury. The authors called it a preliminary study.

name: Scurvy
sx: Tiny bleeding spots around hair follicles
Easy bruising and poor wound healing
about: Vitamin C is needed to build stable collagen, the protein that holds blood vessels, gums and skin together. Without it, vessels leak and wounds reopen. In 1747 the naval surgeon James Lind ran one of the first controlled clinical trials and found that citrus fruit cured scurvy in sailors.

study.title: Adult scurvy
study.note: A case report of three patients showing that scurvy can mimic deep vein thrombosis, vasculitis or bleeding disorders and often leads to extensive tests for the wrong diagnosis.

name: Atrial fibrillation
sx: Fluttering or pounding in the chest
about: The upper chambers of the heart (atria) quiver chaotically instead of contracting, so the heartbeat becomes irregular. Blood can pool in a pouch of the left atrium and form clots, which is why atrial fibrillation raises stroke risk about fivefold and many patients take blood thinners. Some people have no symptoms at all.

study.title: Long-Term Anticoagulation Discontinuation After Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation: The ALONE-AF Randomized Clinical Trial
study.note: After a successful catheter ablation with no return of the arrhythmia, stopping blood thinners led to fewer combined strokes, embolisms and major bleeds than continuing them.

name: Heart failure
sx: Breathlessness when lying flat, or waking up gasping at night
about: The heart can't pump enough blood to meet the body's needs, either because the muscle is weak or because it is too stiff to fill properly. Pressure backs up into the lungs and veins, so fluid leaks into the lungs and legs. Common causes are heart attacks and long-standing high blood pressure.

study.title: Finerenone in Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction
study.note: In heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved pumping function, finerenone lowered the rate of worsening heart failure events and cardiovascular death compared with placebo.

name: Aortic dissection
sx: Sudden, severe tearing or ripping pain in the chest or back
Pain that moves as the tear spreads
Different blood pressure or pulse in each arm
Stroke-like symptoms such as weakness on one side
about: A tear in the inner lining of the aorta lets blood force its way between the layers of the vessel wall, splitting it apart. It can block branch arteries or rupture, and untreated mortality climbs by the hour. High blood pressure and connective-tissue disorders such as Marfan syndrome raise the risk.

study.title: The International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection (IRAD): new insights into an old disease
study.note: Data from an international registry showed that aortic dissection presents in many ways and classic findings are often missing, so doctors need a high index of suspicion. In-hospital death rates were still high.

name: Pericarditis
sx: Sharp chest pain that improves when sitting up and leaning forward
Chest pain worse when lying down or breathing in
A scratchy rubbing sound over the heart (friction rub)
about: The pericardium, the sac around the heart, becomes inflamed, most often after a viral infection. Its two layers rub against each other, causing sharp pain. Leaning forward eases the pressure on the sac. Fluid can collect around the heart and, rarely, squeeze it (tamponade).

study.title: Phase 3 Trial of Interleukin-1 Trap Rilonacept in Recurrent Pericarditis
study.note: In recurrent pericarditis, the interleukin-1 blocker rilonacept quickly ended flare-ups and greatly lowered the risk of another recurrence compared with placebo.

name: Infective endocarditis
sx: Fever with a new heart murmur
Tiny painless red spots on the palms or soles (Janeway lesions)
Painful lumps on the fingertips (Osler nodes)
Fatigue, night sweats and weight loss
about: Bacteria, often Staphylococcus aureus or streptococci, infect the inner lining and valves of the heart and build clumps called vegetations. Pieces can break off and lodge in small vessels, causing the spots on hands, feet and nails. People with damaged or artificial valves and people who inject drugs are at higher risk.

study.title: Partial Oral versus Intravenous Antibiotic Treatment of Endocarditis
study.note: In stable patients with endocarditis on the left side of the heart, switching from IV to oral antibiotics partway through treatment was noninferior to continuing IV antibiotics.

name: Peripheral artery disease
sx: Calf pain when walking that goes away with rest (claudication)
Weak or absent pulses in the feet
Shiny skin and hair loss on the legs
Sores on the feet that won't heal
about: Fatty plaques narrow the arteries supplying the legs, the same process that causes heart attacks. During walking, muscles need more blood than the narrowed arteries can deliver, so they cramp. Smoking and diabetes are the biggest risk factors.

study.title: Semaglutide and walking capacity in people with symptomatic peripheral artery disease and type 2 diabetes (STRIDE): a phase 3b, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial
study.note: Semaglutide increased walking distance in people with symptomatic peripheral artery disease and type 2 diabetes.

name: Raynaud's phenomenon
sx: Fingers turning white, then blue, then red
Attacks triggered by cold or stress
Numbness or tingling in the fingers or toes
Throbbing or burning as the fingers warm up
about: Small arteries in the fingers and toes clamp down too hard in response to cold or stress, briefly cutting off blood flow (white), leaving oxygen-poor blood (blue), then flushing back (red). Primary Raynaud's is common and harmless. Secondary Raynaud's can signal diseases such as scleroderma or lupus.

study.title: Venodilation in Raynaud's disease
study.note: Found impaired endothelium-dependent widening of veins in people with Raynaud's, possibly from reduced nitric oxide release, which may contribute to the disorder.

name: Aortic stenosis
about: The aortic valve stiffens and narrows, usually from calcium build-up with age, so the heart must push harder to force blood out. The heart muscle thickens and eventually tires. Once symptoms such as chest pain, fainting or breathlessness appear, the outlook without valve replacement is poor.

study.title: Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Replacement for Asymptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis
study.note: In severe aortic stenosis without symptoms, early valve replacement by catheter (TAVR) reduced death, stroke or unplanned cardiac hospitalization compared with watchful waiting.

name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
sx: Breathlessness that slowly worsens over years
about: Long-term exposure to irritants, mainly cigarette smoke, destroys the air sacs (emphysema) and inflames the airways (chronic bronchitis). Air gets trapped in the lungs, so breathing out becomes hard. Unlike asthma, the airflow limitation is not fully reversible.

study.title: Mepolizumab for Eosinophilic Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
study.note: In COPD with high blood eosinophils, the antibody mepolizumab lowered the rate of flare-ups, suggesting eosinophilic inflammation drives some exacerbations.

name: Cystic fibrosis
sx: Poor growth despite a good appetite
about: Mutations in the CFTR gene disrupt the channel that moves chloride and water across cell surfaces. Secretions become thick and sticky, clogging the lungs and pancreas, while sweat becomes extra salty. It is inherited when both parents pass on a faulty copy. The sweat chloride test is the classic diagnostic test.

study.title: Triple Therapy for Cystic Fibrosis Phe508del-Gating and -Residual Function Genotypes
study.note: The three-drug CFTR modulator elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor was effective and safe in patients with additional genotypes and added benefit over earlier modulators.

name: Pneumothorax (collapsed lung)
sx: Sudden sharp chest pain on one side
Reduced breath sounds on one side
about: Air leaks into the space between the lung and chest wall, so the lung partly collapses. Primary spontaneous pneumothorax classically strikes tall, thin young men when small blisters on the lung surface burst. A tension pneumothorax, where trapped air builds pressure, is an emergency.

study.title: Conservative versus Interventional Treatment for Spontaneous Pneumothorax
study.note: For a first spontaneous pneumothorax, watchful waiting was noninferior to inserting a chest drain and caused fewer serious adverse events, though the evidence was described as modest.

name: Bronchiolitis
sx: A baby under 2 with a runny nose that progresses to cough
Brief pauses in breathing in very young infants
about: A viral infection, most often respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), inflames the smallest airways (bronchioles) of infants. Their tiny airways clog easily with mucus and swelling. It is the leading cause of hospitalization in infants in many countries.

study.title: Nirsevimab and Hospitalization for RSV Bronchiolitis
study.note: In real-world use, the long-acting antibody nirsevimab reduced the risk of infants being hospitalized with RSV bronchiolitis.

name: Croup
sx: A high-pitched noise when breathing in (stridor)
about: A viral infection, usually parainfluenza, swells the larynx and trachea in young children. The narrowed airway just below the vocal cords produces the barking cough and stridor. A single dose of a steroid such as dexamethasone reduces the swelling.

study.title: Nebulized budesonide and oral dexamethasone for treatment of croup: a randomized controlled trial
study.note: Oral dexamethasone, nebulized budesonide and both together worked about equally. Oral dexamethasone was preferred because it is easiest, cheapest and most available.

name: Whooping cough (pertussis)
sx: Violent coughing fits followed by a 'whoop' when breathing in
Brief pauses in breathing in babies
about: Bordetella pertussis bacteria release toxins that damage the airway lining and paralyze its cleaning hairs (cilia). It is known in China as the '100-day cough'. It is most dangerous for young babies, which is why pregnant women are offered a vaccine to pass antibodies to the baby.

study.title: Safety and immunogenicity of tetanus diphtheria and acellular pertussis (Tdap) immunization during pregnancy in mothers and infants: a randomized clinical trial
study.note: Giving the Tdap vaccine during pregnancy was not linked to more adverse events, and it gave infants high levels of pertussis antibodies in their first 2 months.

name: Sarcoidosis
sx: Dry cough and shortness of breath
Tender red lumps on the shins (erythema nodosum)
Swollen lymph nodes in the chest seen on X-ray
about: Clusters of immune cells called granulomas form in organs, most often the lungs and lymph nodes. The trigger is unknown. Many cases settle on their own, but some cause lasting lung scarring or affect the heart, eyes or nerves.

study.title: First-Line Treatment of Pulmonary Sarcoidosis with Prednisone or Methotrexate
study.note: As first treatment for pulmonary sarcoidosis, methotrexate was noninferior to prednisone for lung function at 24 weeks, with different side-effect profiles.

name: Obstructive sleep apnea
sx: Pauses in breathing during sleep, noticed by a partner
about: During sleep the throat muscles relax and the airway repeatedly collapses, cutting off breathing until the brain briefly wakes the person. The fragmented sleep causes daytime sleepiness, and the repeated oxygen drops strain the heart. Obesity is the strongest risk factor.

study.title: Tirzepatide for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Obesity
study.note: Tirzepatide reduced breathing interruptions during sleep, body weight and blood pressure in people with moderate-to-severe sleep apnea and obesity.

name: COVID-19
about: Caused by the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus, which enters cells through the ACE2 receptor, found in the airways and many other organs. Sudden loss of smell was especially common with early variants. Severe cases cause pneumonia and blood-clotting problems.

study.title: Safety and Efficacy of the BNT162b2 mRNA Covid-19 Vaccine
study.note: The Pfizer-BioNTech mRNA vaccine gave 95% protection against COVID-19 in people 16 and older, with safety similar to other viral vaccines.

name: Common cold
about: Usually caused by rhinoviruses, along with more than 200 other viruses, that infect the lining of the nose and throat. Symptoms come mostly from the immune response, not the virus itself. Antibiotics don't help, and symptoms usually resolve within about 10 days.

study.title: Social ties and susceptibility to the common cold
study.note: Volunteers deliberately exposed to cold viruses were less likely to develop a cold if they had more diverse social networks.

name: Strep throat
sx: Sudden sore throat with pain on swallowing
Tender swollen glands at the front of the neck
about: Group A Streptococcus bacteria infect the throat, mostly in children aged 5 to 15. The absence of cough helps tell it apart from viral sore throats. Treating it with antibiotics prevents rare but serious complications such as rheumatic fever, which can damage heart valves.

study.title: Treatment of streptococcal pharyngitis revisited
study.note: Reviewed evidence that penicillin shortens strep throat symptoms, prevents complications and limits spread, and looked ahead to rapid strep tests done at the first clinic visit.

name: Sinusitis (rhinosinusitis)
sx: Facial pain or pressure worse when bending forward
Thick yellow or green nasal discharge
Tooth ache in the upper jaw
about: The lining of the air-filled sinuses around the nose swells and blocks drainage, usually after a cold. Most acute cases are viral and clear up without antibiotics. Chronic rhinosinusitis lasts over 12 weeks and can come with nasal polyps.

study.title: Tezepelumab in Adults with Severe Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps
study.note: In severe chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, tezepelumab shrank the polyps, eased congestion and reduced the need for surgery and steroid tablets.

name: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever)
sx: Symptoms that return in the same season each year
about: An IgE-driven allergic reaction to airborne allergens such as pollen, dust mites or pet dander. Mast cells in the nose release histamine, causing sneezing, itching and a runny nose. It often occurs alongside asthma and eczema.

study.title: Acupuncture in patients with seasonal allergic rhinitis: a randomized trial
study.note: Acupuncture improved disease-specific quality of life and antihistamine use compared with sham acupuncture, but the improvements may not be clinically significant.

name: Lung cancer
sx: A cough that won't go away or changes
about: Cells lining the airways grow out of control, most often after years of DNA damage from tobacco smoke. Radon and air pollution also contribute. It is the leading cause of cancer death worldwide, partly because symptoms often appear late. Low-dose CT screening of heavy smokers finds it earlier.

study.title: Efficacy and safety of first-line maintenance therapy with lurbinectedin plus atezolizumab in extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer (IMforte): a randomised, multicentre, open-label, phase 3 trial
study.note: In extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer, adding lurbinectedin to atezolizumab maintenance therapy lengthened survival, with more side effects.

name: Epilepsy
sx: Confusion and sleepiness after an episode
about: The brain is prone to sudden bursts of abnormal, synchronized electrical activity. Where the burst starts determines what happens, from a brief stare to full-body convulsions. Epilepsy is diagnosed after two or more unprovoked seizures, and most people control it with medication.

study.title: Cannabidiol in patients with treatment-resistant epilepsy: an open-label interventional trial
study.note: In an open-label trial, cannabidiol might reduce seizure frequency in children and young adults with highly treatment-resistant epilepsy. The authors called for randomized trials.

name: Alzheimer's disease
about: Sticky amyloid plaques build up between neurons and tangles of tau protein form inside them, and brain cells die, starting in the hippocampus, the memory hub. It is the most common cause of dementia. Alois Alzheimer described the first patient, Auguste Deter, in 1906.

study.title: Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease
study.note: The antibody lecanemab cleared amyloid and produced moderately less decline in cognition and daily function than placebo over 18 months, but with side effects.

name: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)
sx: Progressive weakness in a hand, arm or leg
Thinking and sensation are usually spared
about: Motor neurons in the brain and spinal cord progressively die, so muscles weaken and waste while sensation is usually preserved. Most people die of respiratory failure within a few years. Lou Gehrig, the baseball player, made it famous in the US, and the physicist Stephen Hawking lived with a rare slow form for decades.

study.title: Prognosis for patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: development and validation of a personalised prediction model
study.note: Built and externally validated a model that predicts survival for individual European patients with ALS, intended for counseling and trial design.

name: Guillain-Barré syndrome
sx: Weakness that starts in the legs and climbs upward over days
Tingling in the feet and hands
Recent stomach bug or respiratory infection
about: After an infection, often Campylobacter food poisoning, the immune system mistakenly attacks the peripheral nerves. Weakness can progress to paralysis of the breathing muscles, so patients are watched closely. Most recover over months with treatment such as immunoglobulin or plasma exchange.

study.title: Risk of Guillain-Barré Syndrome Following Recombinant Zoster Vaccine in Medicare Beneficiaries
study.note: Found a slightly increased risk of Guillain-Barré syndrome in the 42 days after the recombinant shingles vaccine, about 3 extra cases per million doses, to be weighed against the vaccine's benefits.

name: Myasthenia gravis
sx: Muscle weakness that worsens with use and improves with rest
Weak neck or arms by the end of the day
about: Antibodies block or destroy the acetylcholine receptors where nerves signal muscles, so repeated use quickly exhausts the muscle. Eye muscles are often hit first. The thymus gland is often abnormal, and removing it can help.

study.title: A Phase 3 Trial of Inebilizumab in Generalized Myasthenia Gravis
study.note: In generalized myasthenia gravis with AChR or MuSK antibodies, the B-cell-depleting drug inebilizumab improved function and reduced disease severity.

name: Cluster headache
sx: Attacks lasting 15 minutes to 3 hours, often at the same time each day
Red, watering eye on the same side
Runny or blocked nostril on the painful side
about: Among the most painful conditions known. The hypothalamus, the brain's internal clock, appears to set off attacks, which is why they come in bouts with clockwork timing. The pain activates nerves that also make the eye water and nose run on that side. Breathing high-flow oxygen can stop an attack.

study.title: Long-term safety, tolerability, and efficacy of eptinezumab in chronic cluster headache (CHRONICLE): an open-label safety trial
study.note: In an open-label safety trial, the anti-CGRP antibody eptinezumab was generally well tolerated over 12 months in chronic cluster headache. Randomized trials are needed to confirm benefit.

name: Trigeminal neuralgia
sx: Brief, electric-shock-like stabs of pain in the face
Pain on one side of the jaw, cheek or lip
Attacks triggered by light touch, chewing, talking or brushing teeth
about: The trigeminal nerve, which carries sensation from the face, misfires, often because a blood vessel presses on it near the brainstem and wears away its insulation. Anti-seizure drugs such as carbamazepine are first-line treatment.

study.title: Safety and efficacy of erenumab in patients with trigeminal neuralgia in Denmark: a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, proof-of-concept study
study.note: The anti-CGRP antibody erenumab did not reduce pain compared with placebo, suggesting CGRP plays little role in this paroxysmal pain.

name: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
sx: A sudden 'thunderclap' headache, the worst of one's life
Brief loss of consciousness or seizure
about: Bleeding into the space around the brain, most often from a ruptured berry aneurysm at the base of the brain. Blood irritates the meninges and raises pressure inside the skull. Days later, the arteries can spasm and starve the brain of blood.

study.title: Cerebral arterial spasm--a controlled trial of nimodipine in patients with subarachnoid hemorrhage
study.note: Nimodipine reduced severe neurological deficits from artery spasm after subarachnoid hemorrhage. Nimodipine is still standard care today.

name: Concussion
sx: Headache after a blow to the head
Nausea and sensitivity to light or noise
about: A blow or jolt shakes the brain inside the skull, stretching nerve fibers and causing a temporary energy crisis in brain cells. Most people recover within weeks with rest followed by a gradual return to activity. A second blow before recovery can be more dangerous.

study.title: Relationship between concussion and neuropsychological performance in college football players
study.note: College football players with multiple past concussions, especially those with learning disabilities, performed worse on neuropsychological tests.

name: Huntington's disease
sx: A parent with the same condition
about: An inherited disease caused by an expanded CAG repeat in the HTT gene, producing a toxic huntingtin protein that kills neurons in the basal ganglia. Each child of an affected parent has a 50% chance of inheriting it. Symptoms usually begin in mid-adulthood.

study.title: Targeting Huntingtin Expression in Patients with Huntington's Disease
study.note: An antisense drug (tominersen) injected into the spinal fluid lowered mutant huntingtin levels in a dose-dependent way without serious adverse events.

name: Restless legs syndrome
sx: An irresistible urge to move the legs
Creeping or crawling sensations in the legs
Symptoms worse in the evening and at night
about: Thought to involve disrupted dopamine signaling and low iron in the brain. Iron deficiency, pregnancy and kidney failure make it more likely. It is linked to periodic limb movements during sleep.

study.title: Comparison of pregabalin with pramipexole for restless legs syndrome
study.note: Pregabalin worked better than placebo and caused less 'augmentation', a drug-induced worsening of symptoms, than the dopamine drug pramipexole.

name: Narcolepsy
sx: Overwhelming daytime sleepiness and sudden sleep attacks
Sudden muscle weakness triggered by laughter or strong emotion (cataplexy)
Vivid dreams when falling asleep or waking
about: In narcolepsy type 1, the brain loses the hypothalamic neurons that make orexin (hypocretin), a chemical that keeps us awake. Without it, pieces of dream (REM) sleep intrude into waking life, including the muscle paralysis of dreaming, which causes cataplexy.

study.title: Oveporexton, an Oral Orexin Receptor 2-Selective Agonist, in Narcolepsy Type 1
study.note: An orexin-receptor-2 agonist, oveporexton, improved wakefulness, sleepiness and cataplexy over 8 weeks in narcolepsy type 1, directly replacing the missing signal.

name: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV)
sx: Brief spinning dizziness triggered by turning the head or rolling over in bed
Episodes lasting less than a minute
about: Tiny calcium carbonate crystals (otoconia) break loose in the inner ear and drift into a semicircular canal. When the head moves, they slosh around and falsely signal spinning. A simple head-repositioning maneuver, the Epley maneuver, moves them back and often cures it.

study.title: Prevention of benign paroxysmal positional vertigo with vitamin D supplementation: A randomized trial
study.note: Vitamin D and calcium supplements reduced recurrences of BPPV, especially in people with low vitamin D levels.

name: Ménière's disease
sx: Attacks of spinning vertigo lasting 20 minutes to hours
Fluctuating hearing loss in one ear
A feeling of fullness or pressure in the ear
about: Thought to involve a build-up of fluid (endolymphatic hydrops) in the inner ear, which disrupts both balance and hearing organs. Over years, hearing in the affected ear may permanently decline.

study.title: Efficacy and safety of betahistine treatment in patients with Meniere's disease: primary results of a long term, multicentre, double blind, randomised, placebo controlled, dose defining trial (BEMED trial)
study.note: In a large long-term trial, betahistine, a widely prescribed drug for Ménière's disease, did not reduce vertigo attacks more than placebo.

name: Sciatica
sx: Pain shooting from the lower back down the back of one leg
Numbness or tingling in the leg or foot
Pain worse when sitting, coughing or sneezing
Weakness in the leg or foot
about: A nerve root of the sciatic nerve is compressed or inflamed, most often by a herniated disc in the lower spine. Raising the straight leg stretches the nerve and reproduces the pain, which is a classic bedside test. Most cases improve within weeks.

study.title: Acupuncture vs Sham Acupuncture for Chronic Sciatica From Herniated Disk: A Randomized Clinical Trial
study.note: In chronic sciatica from a herniated disc, acupuncture reduced pain and improved function compared with sham acupuncture, with benefits lasting a year.

name: Herpes simplex encephalitis
about: Herpes simplex virus infects the brain itself, typically the temporal lobes, which handle memory, smell and language. It is the most common cause of sporadic fatal encephalitis. Starting the antiviral acyclovir quickly greatly improves survival.

study.title: Frequency, symptoms, risk factors, and outcomes of autoimmune encephalitis after herpes simplex encephalitis: a prospective observational study and retrospective analysis
study.note: About 27% of patients developed autoimmune encephalitis after herpes simplex encephalitis, usually within 2 months, linked to new antibodies against neurons.

name: Type 2 diabetes
sx: Increased thirst and urination that come on gradually
Dark velvety skin patches in the neck or armpits
about: The body's cells stop responding well to insulin (insulin resistance), and the pancreas eventually can't keep up, so blood sugar rises. It develops slowly and is strongly linked to excess weight and genetics. Many people have no symptoms for years.

study.title: Primary care-led weight management for remission of type 2 diabetes (DiRECT): an open-label, cluster-randomised trial
study.note: In a primary-care weight-management program, almost half of participants reached remission of type 2 diabetes at 12 months while off diabetes medicines.

name: Primary hyperparathyroidism
sx: Fatigue, low mood and poor concentration
about: A parathyroid gland, usually a single benign adenoma, overproduces parathyroid hormone, pulling calcium out of bones and raising blood calcium. Medical students remember the symptoms as 'stones, bones, abdominal groans and psychic moans'. Today it is mostly found on routine blood tests.

study.title: Risk of Fracture Among Older Adults With Primary Hyperparathyroidism Receiving Parathyroidectomy vs Nonoperative Management
study.note: Among older adults, parathyroid surgery was associated with a lower risk of fractures, including hip fractures, than nonoperative management.

name: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
about: A hormonal disorder with excess androgens (male-type hormones), irregular ovulation and many small follicles on the ovaries. Insulin resistance is common and drives androgen production. It is one of the most common causes of infertility.

study.title: Myo-inositol Supplementation to Prevent Pregnancy Complications in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Randomized Clinical Trial
study.note: Myo-inositol supplements during pregnancy did not reduce a combination of gestational diabetes, preeclampsia or preterm birth in women with PCOS.

name: Acromegaly
sx: Enlarging hands and feet: rings and shoes no longer fit
Coarsening facial features with a protruding jaw and brow
about: A pituitary tumor makes too much growth hormone in adulthood, after the growth plates have closed. Bones can't lengthen, so they thicken instead and soft tissues enlarge. In children, before growth plates close, the same excess causes gigantism.

study.title: Gigantism and acromegaly due to Xq26 microduplications and GPR101 mutation
study.note: Discovered X-linked acrogigantism, an early-childhood form of gigantism caused by a duplication involving the GPR101 gene, also mutated in some adults with acromegaly.

name: Pheochromocytoma
sx: Very high blood pressure, often in spikes
about: A rare tumor of the adrenal medulla that releases bursts of adrenaline and noradrenaline. The classic triad is headache, sweating and palpitations. It is often called the '10% tumor', although more are now known to be hereditary than that rule suggests.

study.title: Belzutifan for Advanced Pheochromocytoma or Paraganglioma
study.note: Belzutifan, a HIF-2α inhibitor, produced durable tumor responses in people with advanced pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma.

name: Diabetes insipidus
sx: Passing large volumes of very dilute urine
Extreme thirst, often for ice-cold water
about: Not related to blood sugar. The body lacks vasopressin (antidiuretic hormone) or the kidneys don't respond to it, so they can't concentrate urine and pour out water. 'Insipidus' means tasteless, as opposed to the sweet urine of diabetes mellitus. In 2022 experts proposed renaming the central form arginine vasopressin deficiency.

study.title: A Copeptin-Based Approach in the Diagnosis of Diabetes Insipidus
study.note: Measuring the hormone marker copeptin after a hypertonic saline infusion diagnosed diabetes insipidus more accurately than the classic water-deprivation test.

name: Hypoglycemia
sx: Seizures or loss of consciousness if severe
about: Blood glucose drops too low, usually in people taking insulin or certain diabetes drugs. The brain depends on glucose, so thinking falters, and the body releases adrenaline, causing shakiness and sweating. Fast-acting sugar treats it, and glucagon is used when the person can't swallow.

study.title: Effect of Continuous Glucose Monitoring on Hypoglycemia in Older Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: A Randomized Clinical Trial
study.note: In adults aged 60 and over with type 1 diabetes, continuous glucose monitoring produced a small but significant reduction in hypoglycemia over 6 months.

name: Osteoporosis
sx: Bones that break from a minor fall
Sudden back pain from a spinal fracture
about: Bone is broken down faster than it is rebuilt, leaving bones porous and fragile. Estrogen loss after menopause speeds bone breakdown, so it is most common in older women. It is often silent until a fracture of the hip, wrist or spine. It is diagnosed with a DEXA bone density scan.

study.title: Romosozumab or Alendronate for Fracture Prevention in Women with Osteoporosis
study.note: In postmenopausal women at high fracture risk, a year of romosozumab followed by alendronate cut fracture risk more than alendronate alone.

name: Crohn's disease
sx: Fistulas or abscesses near the anus
about: A form of inflammatory bowel disease in which inflammation can strike anywhere from mouth to anus, in patches, and through the full thickness of the bowel wall. That deep inflammation can create tunnels (fistulas) and narrowings. The end of the small intestine is the most common site.

study.title: Upadacitinib Induction and Maintenance Therapy for Crohn's Disease
study.note: The JAK inhibitor upadacitinib was superior to placebo for both inducing and maintaining remission in moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease.

name: Ulcerative colitis
sx: Urgent need to go to the toilet
about: A form of inflammatory bowel disease limited to the colon. Inflammation starts at the rectum and spreads continuously upward, affecting only the inner lining. Long-standing disease raises colon cancer risk, so patients get regular colonoscopies.

study.title: Risankizumab for Ulcerative Colitis: Two Randomized Clinical Trials
study.note: The IL-23 blocker risankizumab improved remission rates compared with placebo in both induction and maintenance trials for moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis.

name: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)
sx: Recurring abdominal pain relieved by a bowel movement
Symptoms flare with stress or certain foods
about: A disorder of gut-brain interaction: the bowel looks normal, but its nerves are oversensitive and its movements irregular. It is diagnosed by symptom pattern after ruling out red flags such as bleeding or weight loss. Diet changes such as low-FODMAP can help.

study.title: The Mediterranean Diet for Irritable Bowel Syndrome : A Randomized Clinical Trial
study.note: A Mediterranean diet was noninferior and superior to traditional dietary advice for managing IBS symptoms.

name: Diverticulitis
sx: Pain in the lower left abdomen
about: Small pouches (diverticula) that bulge out of the colon wall, very common with age, become inflamed or infected. In Western countries they mostly form in the sigmoid colon, which is why the pain is usually on the lower left. CT scanning confirms the diagnosis.

study.title: Diet and Risk for Incident Diverticulitis in Women : A Prospective Cohort Study
study.note: Healthier diets were associated with lower risk of diverticulitis in women, and eating nuts and seeds was not linked to higher risk, contrary to old advice.

name: Acute pancreatitis
sx: Severe upper abdominal pain boring through to the back
Recent heavy drinking or known gallstones
about: Digestive enzymes activate too early inside the pancreas and begin digesting the gland itself. Gallstones and heavy alcohol use cause most cases. Blood tests show high lipase or amylase. Severe cases can trigger organ failure.

study.title: Aggressive or Moderate Fluid Resuscitation in Acute Pancreatitis
study.note: Early aggressive IV fluids for acute pancreatitis caused more fluid overload without improving outcomes compared with moderate fluids, which changed practice.

name: Cirrhosis
sx: Yellowing of the skin and eyes (jaundice)
Spider-like blood vessels on the skin
about: Years of liver damage from alcohol, viral hepatitis or fatty liver disease replace healthy tissue with scar tissue. Blood backs up in the portal vein, causing fluid build-up and swollen veins in the esophagus that can bleed. The failing liver can't clear toxins, which reach the brain and cause confusion.

study.title: Simvastatin and Rifaximin in Decompensated Cirrhosis: A Randomized Clinical Trial
study.note: Adding simvastatin and rifaximin to standard therapy did not improve outcomes in decompensated cirrhosis.

name: Hepatitis A
sx: Yellowing of the skin and eyes
about: A virus spread through contaminated food or water (fecal-oral route) that inflames the liver. Unlike hepatitis B and C, it never becomes chronic, and young children often have no symptoms. A vaccine prevents it.

study.title: Protection against hepatitis A by an inactivated vaccine
study.note: An inactivated hepatitis A vaccine was safe and, given in two doses, protected against hepatitis A for at least a year.

name: Viral gastroenteritis (stomach flu)
sx: Others nearby falling ill at the same time
about: Viruses such as norovirus and rotavirus infect the intestines. Norovirus is extremely contagious, since a handful of particles can cause infection, and it causes outbreaks on cruise ships and in care homes. The main danger is dehydration, which oral rehydration solution treats.

study.title: Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG versus Placebo for Acute Gastroenteritis in Children
study.note: Among preschool children with acute gastroenteritis, a 5-day course of the probiotic Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG did not improve outcomes compared with placebo.

name: Bowel obstruction
sx: Cramping abdominal pain that comes in waves
Unable to pass stool or gas
about: Something blocks the intestine, most often scar tissue (adhesions) from previous surgery, a hernia or a tumor. Gas and fluid build up behind the blockage and the bowel wall can lose its blood supply. Green (bilious) vomiting in a newborn is a surgical emergency.

study.title: Colour of bile vomiting in intestinal obstruction in the newborn: questionnaire study
study.note: Many parents and GPs did not recognize green as the color of bile in a newborn's vomit, which could delay urgent surgical referral for intestinal obstruction.

name: Hemorrhoids
sx: Bright red blood on toilet paper or in the bowl
Pain when sitting, if a clot forms
about: Cushions of blood vessels in the anal canal swell and slip downward, often from straining, constipation or pregnancy. Internal hemorrhoids usually bleed painlessly, while external ones can clot and hurt.

study.title: Anorectal varices, haemorrhoids, and portal hypertension
study.note: In patients with liver disease, hemorrhoids occurred independently of anorectal varices and portal pressure, showing they are distinct conditions that both can bleed.

name: Lactose intolerance
about: Most of the world's adults produce less lactase, the enzyme that splits milk sugar, after childhood. Undigested lactose reaches the colon, where bacteria ferment it into gas and draw in water. Continuing to make lactase into adulthood (lactase persistence) evolved separately in several dairying populations.

study.title: Recurrent abdominal pain of childhood due to lactose intolerance
study.note: Lactose malabsorption contributed to recurrent abdominal pain in children: 70% of those with malabsorption had more frequent pain when lactose went back into their diet.

name: Achalasia
sx: Difficulty swallowing both solids and liquids
about: Nerves in the esophagus wall degenerate, so the lower esophageal sphincter fails to relax and the esophagus loses its squeezing waves. Food piles up, and a barium swallow shows a classic 'bird's beak' narrowing.

study.title: Endoscopic or Surgical Myotomy in Patients with Idiopathic Achalasia
study.note: Endoscopic myotomy (POEM) was noninferior to laparoscopic surgery for controlling achalasia symptoms at 2 years, though reflux was more common after POEM.

name: Colorectal cancer
sx: A change in bowel habits lasting weeks
about: Most colorectal cancers grow slowly from benign polyps over about 10 years, which is why removing polyps during colonoscopy prevents cancer. Risk rises with age, family history, red and processed meat and inflammatory bowel disease, and rates are climbing in younger adults.

study.title: Low-Dose Aspirin for PI3K-Altered Localized Colorectal Cancer
study.note: Low-dose aspirin lowered colorectal cancer recurrence compared with placebo in patients whose tumors carried PI3K-pathway mutations.

name: Pyloric stenosis
sx: Forceful projectile vomiting after feeds in a baby a few weeks old
Baby hungry again right after vomiting
An olive-sized lump in the upper abdomen
about: The muscle of the pylorus, the outlet of the stomach, thickens in the first weeks of life, blocking food from passing into the intestine. It is more common in firstborn boys. A short operation (pyloromyotomy) cures it.

study.title: Familial aggregation and heritability of pyloric stenosis
study.note: In Danish children, pyloric stenosis showed strong clustering in families and high heritability.

name: Intussusception
sx: Sudden bouts of severe crying with knees drawn up, every 15-20 minutes
A sausage-shaped lump in the abdomen
about: One part of the intestine telescopes into the next, most often in infants and toddlers. The trapped bowel swells and loses blood supply, producing the classic jelly-like bloody stool. An air or contrast enema can often push it back without surgery.

study.title: Intussusception after Rotavirus Vaccine Introduction in India
study.note: An Indian-made rotavirus vaccine was not associated with intussusception in Indian infants, an important safety question because an early rotavirus vaccine was withdrawn over this risk.

name: Urinary tract infection (cystitis)
sx: Needing to urinate often and urgently
about: Bacteria, usually E. coli from the gut, travel up the urethra into the bladder. Women get UTIs far more often because their urethra is much shorter. Spread to the kidneys causes pyelonephritis.

study.title: Oral gepotidacin versus nitrofurantoin in patients with uncomplicated urinary tract infection (EAGLE-2 and EAGLE-3): two randomised, controlled, double-blind, double-dummy, phase 3, non-inferiority trials
study.note: A first-in-class oral antibiotic, gepotidacin, was effective for uncomplicated urinary tract infections compared with nitrofurantoin, including against some drug-resistant bacteria.

name: Pyelonephritis (kidney infection)
sx: Pain in the side or back
Tenderness when the back is tapped over the kidney
about: A bladder infection climbs up the ureters into the kidneys. It is more serious than cystitis and can spread to the bloodstream (urosepsis). It needs prompt antibiotics.

study.title: Effect of Cefepime/Enmetazobactam vs Piperacillin/Tazobactam on Clinical Cure and Microbiological Eradication in Patients With Complicated Urinary Tract Infection or Acute Pyelonephritis: A Randomized Clinical Trial
study.note: For complicated UTIs and acute pyelonephritis, cefepime-enmetazobactam was noninferior and superior to piperacillin-tazobactam for cure and bacterial clearance.

name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
sx: Getting up at night to urinate
about: The prostate gland grows with age under the influence of hormones and squeezes the urethra that runs through it. It is not cancer and does not cause cancer. Severe cases can cause sudden inability to urinate (acute retention).

study.title: The long-term effect of doxazosin, finasteride, and combination therapy on the clinical progression of benign prostatic hyperplasia
study.note: Long-term combination therapy with doxazosin and finasteride reduced progression of BPH more than either drug alone, including lowering the risk of urinary retention and surgery.

name: Testicular torsion
sx: Sudden severe pain in one testicle
The testicle sitting higher than normal
Loss of the normal reflex when the inner thigh is stroked
about: The testicle twists on its spermatic cord, cutting off its blood supply, most often in teenage boys. It is a surgical emergency: the chance of saving the testicle falls sharply after about 6 hours.

study.title: The diagnosis of testicular torsion
study.note: Telling torsion from epididymitis is hard because of overlapping ages and symptoms. Imaging helps but should not delay surgery, and epididymitis should be diagnosed cautiously in men under 35.

name: Ectopic pregnancy
sx: A missed period or positive pregnancy test
Dizziness or fainting if it ruptures
about: A fertilized egg implants outside the uterus, usually in a fallopian tube, which cannot stretch to hold it. A rupture causes internal bleeding. Blood irritating the diaphragm can cause pain felt in the shoulder tip. It is a leading cause of pregnancy-related death in the first trimester.

study.title: Ectopic pregnancy and occupational exposure to antineoplastic drugs
study.note: Nurses occupationally exposed to anticancer drugs had higher odds of ectopic pregnancy. The authors cautioned that the numbers were small and needed confirmation.

name: Endometriosis
sx: Painful bowel movements or urination during periods
about: Tissue similar to the uterine lining grows outside the uterus, on the ovaries, bowel or pelvic lining, and bleeds and inflames with each cycle. Diagnosis often takes years. It affects roughly 1 in 10 women of reproductive age.

study.title: Endometriosis Typology and Ovarian Cancer Risk
study.note: Ovarian cancer risk was markedly higher in women with ovarian endometriomas or deep infiltrating endometriosis.

name: Preeclampsia
sx: High blood pressure after 20 weeks of pregnancy
Vision changes such as flashing lights
Sudden swelling of the face and hands
about: The placenta develops abnormal blood vessels and releases factors that damage the mother's blood vessel linings, raising blood pressure and harming the kidneys, liver and brain. Delivery of the placenta is the only cure. Untreated, it can progress to seizures (eclampsia).

study.title: Aspirin versus Placebo in Pregnancies at High Risk for Preterm Preeclampsia
study.note: Low-dose aspirin given to women at high risk lowered the rate of preterm preeclampsia compared with placebo (the ASPRE trial).

name: Polycystic kidney disease
sx: High blood pressure at a young age
Enlarged kidneys felt in the abdomen
A family history of kidney disease
about: Inherited mutations, usually in PKD1 or PKD2, cause fluid-filled cysts to grow throughout both kidneys, gradually crowding out working tissue. Many patients eventually need dialysis or a transplant. Some also have brain aneurysms.

study.title: Tolvaptan in patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
study.note: Tolvaptan slowed kidney growth and the decline in kidney function over 3 years, but more patients stopped it because of side effects.

name: Sickle cell disease
sx: Sudden episodes of severe pain (pain crises)
Painful swelling of the hands and feet in young children
about: A single-letter change in the hemoglobin gene makes red blood cells stiffen into a sickle shape when they release oxygen. Sickled cells block small vessels, causing pain and organ damage, and they break down early, causing anemia. Carrying one copy protects against severe malaria, which is why it is common where malaria is.

study.title: CRISPR-Cas9 Gene Editing for Sickle Cell Disease and β-Thalassemia
study.note: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing that switches fetal hemoglobin back on made two patients transfusion-independent and, in the patient with sickle cell disease, stopped pain crises.

name: Hemophilia
sx: Bleeding into joints, causing pain and swelling
Prolonged bleeding after cuts, dental work or surgery
about: An inherited lack of clotting factor VIII (hemophilia A) or IX (hemophilia B). The genes are on the X chromosome, so it mostly affects males. It famously ran in the descendants of Queen Victoria, including the Russian royal family.

study.title: Emicizumab Prophylaxis in Hemophilia A with Inhibitors
study.note: Emicizumab, an antibody that mimics factor VIII, sharply cut bleeding episodes in hemophilia A patients whose bodies had made inhibitors against standard factor treatment.

name: Vitamin B12 deficiency (pernicious anemia)
sx: Tingling or numbness in hands and feet
about: B12 is needed to make DNA for red blood cells and to maintain the myelin around nerves, so deficiency causes large, immature red cells and nerve damage. In pernicious anemia, an autoimmune attack destroys the stomach cells that make intrinsic factor, the protein needed to absorb B12.

study.title: Iron deficiency occurs frequently in patients with pernicious anemia
study.note: Patients with pernicious anemia were often also iron deficient, at diagnosis or later, so routine iron checks were recommended.

name: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia
sx: Easy bruising and tiny red spots on the skin
about: Immature white blood cells (lymphoblasts) multiply out of control in the bone marrow, crowding out normal red cells, platelets and infection-fighting cells. It is the most common childhood cancer, and about 90% of children are now cured, one of medicine's biggest success stories.

study.title: Blinatumomab for MRD-Negative Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia in Adults
study.note: Adding the immunotherapy blinatumomab to chemotherapy improved survival in adults with B-cell ALL already in deep remission.

name: Hodgkin lymphoma
sx: A painless swollen lymph node in the neck
about: A cancer of the lymphatic system marked by large abnormal cells called Reed-Sternberg cells. It often strikes young adults and is one of the most curable cancers. Fever, night sweats and weight loss are called 'B symptoms' and signal more widespread disease.

study.title: Nivolumab+AVD in Advanced-Stage Classic Hodgkin's Lymphoma
study.note: Nivolumab plus chemotherapy (AVD) gave longer progression-free survival and fewer side effects than brentuximab vedotin plus AVD in advanced Hodgkin lymphoma.

name: Multiple myeloma
sx: Bone pain, especially in the back or ribs
Thirst and confusion from high calcium
about: A cancer of plasma cells, the antibody factories of the bone marrow. They make huge amounts of one useless antibody and dissolve bone, causing the CRAB features: high Calcium, Renal failure, Anemia and Bone lesions.

study.title: Daratumumab, Bortezomib, Lenalidomide, and Dexamethasone for Multiple Myeloma
study.note: Adding daratumumab to standard induction, consolidation and maintenance therapy significantly prolonged progression-free survival in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma.

name: Polycythemia vera
sx: Itching after a warm bath or shower
Burning pain in the hands and feet
about: A bone marrow cancer, usually driven by a JAK2 gene mutation, that makes too many red blood cells. The blood becomes thick, raising clot risk. Regularly removing blood (venesection), the modern version of bloodletting, is a mainstay of treatment.

study.title: Ruxolitinib versus standard therapy for the treatment of polycythemia vera
study.note: In patients who did not respond to or tolerate hydroxyurea, the JAK inhibitor ruxolitinib controlled blood counts, shrank the spleen and eased symptoms better than standard therapy.

name: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP)
sx: Pinpoint red-purple spots on the skin (petechiae)
about: The immune system makes antibodies against platelets, which the spleen then destroys, so blood can't clot properly. In children it often follows a viral infection and clears up on its own. In adults it is more often chronic.

study.title: Ianalumab plus Eltrombopag in Immune Thrombocytopenia
study.note: Adding the antibody ianalumab to eltrombopag delayed treatment failure in immune thrombocytopenia compared with eltrombopag alone.

name: Hereditary hemochromatosis
sx: Joint pain, often in the knuckles of the index and middle fingers
about: An inherited condition, most often from two copies of the C282Y variant in the HFE gene, in which the gut absorbs too much iron. Iron slowly builds up in the liver, pancreas, heart, joints and skin. Regular blood removal treats it. It is one of the most common genetic conditions in people of Northern European descent.

study.title: Association of Hemochromatosis HFE p.C282Y Homozygosity With Hepatic Malignancy
study.note: Men with two copies of the HFE C282Y variant had a significantly higher risk of liver cancer and death than men without it. No significant link was found in women.

name: Osteoarthritis
sx: Joint pain that worsens with use and eases with rest
Brief stiffness after rest, usually under 30 minutes
A grating or crackling feeling in the joint
Bony lumps on the finger joints
Mostly knees, hips, hands and spine
about: The cartilage cushioning the joint breaks down and the whole joint remodels, with bone spurs and a thickened lining. It is the most common form of arthritis and is closely linked to age, joint injury and excess weight. Exercise is a core treatment.

study.title: Effect of High-Intensity Strength Training on Knee Pain and Knee Joint Compressive Forces Among Adults With Knee Osteoarthritis: The START Randomized Clinical Trial
study.note: High-intensity strength training did not reduce knee pain or joint forces more than low-intensity training or a control group over 18 months.

name: Ankylosing spondylitis
sx: Lower back pain and stiffness that is worse in the morning
Back pain that improves with exercise, not rest
about: Chronic inflammation of the spine and the sacroiliac joints, where the spine meets the pelvis. Over years, inflamed areas can fuse with new bone, creating a 'bamboo spine' on X-ray. Most patients carry the HLA-B27 gene, and it often begins before age 40.

study.title: Secukinumab, an Interleukin-17A Inhibitor, in Ankylosing Spondylitis
study.note: The IL-17A blocker secukinumab significantly reduced the signs and symptoms of ankylosing spondylitis at 16 weeks.

name: Fibromyalgia
sx: Widespread pain on both sides of the body, above and below the waist
about: A chronic pain condition thought to involve 'central sensitization', where the nervous system amplifies pain signals. Blood tests and scans are normal. Exercise and sleep improvement help more than most medicines.

study.title: Effect of tai chi versus aerobic exercise for fibromyalgia: comparative effectiveness randomized controlled trial
study.note: Tai chi improved fibromyalgia symptoms as much as or more than aerobic exercise, with longer practice giving greater benefit.

name: Systemic lupus erythematosus (lupus)
sx: A butterfly-shaped rash across the cheeks and nose
about: An autoimmune disease in which antibodies against the body's own DNA and proteins form immune complexes that inflame skin, joints, kidneys, blood and brain. About 9 in 10 patients are women, often diagnosed between 15 and 45. Antinuclear antibodies (ANA) are present in almost all cases.

study.title: Efficacy and Safety of Obinutuzumab in Active Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
study.note: The B-cell-depleting antibody obinutuzumab outperformed placebo on all primary and key secondary outcomes in active lupus.

name: Polymyalgia rheumatica
sx: Pain and stiffness in both shoulders and upper arms
Pain and stiffness in the hips and thighs
Trouble getting out of bed or raising arms to dress
about: Inflammation around the shoulder and hip joints in people over 50. It responds dramatically to low-dose steroids, often within days. About 1 in 5 also develops giant cell arteritis, so doctors watch for headache and vision changes.

study.title: Phase 3 Trial of Secukinumab in Polymyalgia Rheumatica
study.note: In relapsing polymyalgia rheumatica, adding secukinumab to a steroid taper gave more remissions with lower total steroid doses.

name: Giant cell arteritis
sx: A new headache, often at the temples
Tender scalp, painful to comb the hair
Sudden vision loss or double vision
Over age 50, often with fever and fatigue
about: Inflammation of medium and large arteries, especially branches of the carotid artery in the head. If the artery to the eye closes, blindness can be permanent, so steroids are started immediately, even before a temporal artery biopsy or ultrasound confirms it.

study.title: A Phase 3 Trial of Upadacitinib for Giant-Cell Arteritis
study.note: Upadacitinib 15 mg with a shorter steroid taper sustained remission better than placebo with a longer taper in giant cell arteritis.

name: Plantar fasciitis
sx: Stabbing heel pain with the first steps in the morning
Pain after standing or walking for a long time
Tenderness on the underside of the heel
Pain that eases once warmed up
about: The plantar fascia, a thick band of tissue running from heel to toes, degenerates where it attaches to the heel bone. It is common in runners, people who stand all day and people with flat feet or obesity. Most cases settle with stretching and footwear changes within a year.

study.title: Extracorporeal shock wave therapy for plantar fasciitis: randomised controlled multicentre trial
study.note: Shock-wave therapy was ineffective for chronic plantar fasciitis in a multicenter randomized trial.

name: Tennis elbow (lateral epicondylitis)
sx: Pain on the outside of the elbow
Pain when shaking hands or turning a doorknob
about: Overuse damages the tendon that attaches forearm muscles to the outer elbow, causing tendon degeneration rather than true inflammation. Despite the name, most cases occur in people who don't play tennis.

study.title: Mobilisation with movement and exercise, corticosteroid injection, or wait and see for tennis elbow: randomised trial
study.note: Steroid injections helped in the short term, but after 6 weeks they did worse than physiotherapy, with high recurrence rates.

name: Osteomyelitis
sx: Warmth and swelling over the bone
A child refusing to use a limb or bear weight
A wound or ulcer that won't heal over the bone
about: Infection of bone, most often by Staphylococcus aureus, spreading through the blood (common in children) or from a nearby wound (common in diabetic foot ulcers). Bone's limited blood supply makes it hard for antibiotics to reach, so treatment lasts weeks.

study.title: Antibiotic treatment for 6 weeks versus 12 weeks in patients with pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis: an open-label, non-inferiority, randomised, controlled trial
